findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored unencrypted at rest by default (SSE not enforced), risking exposure of sensitive data if underlying storage or backups are compromised.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl is specified and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated, so the bucket may default to being accessible in ways not explicitly restricted, and there is no explicit denial of public access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger/financial export data, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive infrastructure details or credentials) unencrypted at rest.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL, which grants the S3 log delivery group write and read-ACP permissions; combined with no public access block, this could allow broader access than intended to audit log data if not carefully scoped.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption at rest / no explicit KMS
findings.description: The uploaded object does not specify server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), so it inherits the bucket's lack of default encryption, exposing the vendor roster file (likely containing PII/vendor data) unencrypted at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without manual emptying, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irrecoverable data loss/deletion if misused or via compromised credentials.
